articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the September 1991 issue (Volume 3, Number 9) of "Ephemeris," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It serves as a record of the association's activities and news for that specific month.

articles.title: AUGUST MEETING
articles.summary: The August "Eclipse Night" meeting was a great success, drawing over 100 members and eclipse enthusiasts. Numerous striking slides showcasing various aspects of the eclipse were presented, and special thanks were given to all contributors.

articles.title: FIELD OF VIEW
articles.summary: The SJAA is holding its annual picnic and Bar-B-Q at Fremont Peak State Park, starting at 4 pm with observing afterward. Members should note that the General Meeting date has been moved to September 14th for the annual slide and equipment night, and the Introductory Astronomy Class is now on September 21st.

articles.title: EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
articles.summary: The article announces an employment opportunity for a new Editor of the 'Ephemeris' publication, as the current editor is stepping down after 7 years. It also details a packed schedule of upcoming events for September and October, including SJAA picnics, star parties at various locations, general meetings, and public star parties.

articles.title: TELESCOPE MAKING AND ASTRONOMY
articles.summary: This article announces the renewal period for 'Telescope Making' and 'Astronomy' magazines, noting that subscribers can renew through the SJAA or individually. It also informs readers of increased subscription prices, now $10 for 'Telescope Making' and $16 for 'Astronomy', and provides contact details for renewals.

articles.title: SEPTEMBER STARRY NIGHTS
articles.summary: Richard Stanton recounts meeting a young, aspiring amateur astronomer in the Midwest who, despite having a telescope, lacked basic information and resources to begin due to living outside a major metropolitan area and having parents without a science background. The author highlights this as a significant failing of the amateur astronomy community and stresses the responsibility of experienced enthusiasts to provide guidance, resources, and outreach to beginners.

articles.title: DOUBLE, TRIPLE, AND MULTIPLE STARS
articles.summary: Patrick M. Donnelly shares his personal experience and renewed interest in observing multiple star systems, particularly those designated with 'Gamma,' which he dubs the 'Gamma Gang.' The article details several notable examples, including Gamma Leonis, Gamma Virginis, Gamma Andromedae (Almach), Gamma Delphinus, and Gamma Arietis, providing their characteristics, visibility, and observational tips. The author encourages readers to explore and observe these beautiful double, triple, and multiple star systems.

articles.title: SPACE PROGRAM UPDATE
articles.summary: This article provides an update on the 1991 space program, detailing completed Space Shuttle missions including satellite deployments and scientific experiments, as well as upcoming missions. It also reports on the survival of the Space Station program in Congress for FY 1992 despite budget cuts that led to the cancellation of the Comet Rendezvous Asteroid Flyby mission and delays for Cassini and the Advanced X-ray Astrophysics Facility. Furthermore, the Hubble Space Telescope is experiencing significant gyro problems, potentially necessitating a shuttle repair mission.

articles.title: SOLAR ARRAYS WILL NOT BE READY FOR LAUNCH
articles.summary: The launch, likely related to Hubble, will be delayed until late 1993 because the necessary solar arrays are not yet ready. Additionally, the Hubble Space Telescope is equipped with a backup 'retrieval mode' gyro pack to mitigate the risk of a complete failure of its main gyros.

articles.title: U.S./SOVIET SPACE AGREEMENT SIGNED A THE MOSCOW SUMMIT
articles.summary: Presidents Bush and Gorbachev signed a U.S./Soviet space agreement on July 31 at the Moscow Summit. This landmark agreement outlined plans for a U.S. astronaut to fly on a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft to the Mir space station for up to six months, and a Soviet cosmonaut to participate in a U.S. Space Shuttle/Spacelab flight.

articles.title: U.S. EXPERIENCING WEATHER SATELLITE PROBLEMS
articles.summary: The U.S. is facing significant issues with its geostationary weather satellite system, as GOES East has failed and the next-generation GOES Next is experiencing development problems. To compensate, the European Meteosat 9 has been relocated to cover Brazil and replace GOES East. Additionally, the European Meteosat 3 is being utilized as an orbital spare with an expected operational lifespan extending into late 1993 or early 1994.

articles.title: EUROPEAN EARTH-RESOURCES SATELLITE LAUNCHED
articles.summary: The European Earth-resources satellite, ERS-1, was successfully launched on July 16 using an Ariane 4 booster. This mission is expected to position the European Space Agency (ESA) at the forefront of ocean-based research in climatology and meteorology.

articles.title: SECOND PEGASUS LAUNCHED SUCCESSFULLY
articles.summary: The article reports on the successful launch of the second Pegasus booster on July 17, which placed seven small satellites into orbit. It then vividly describes an observation of a total solar eclipse, lasting 6 minutes and 43 seconds, from a ship near Mazatlan. Key features noted were the bright sky, streamered corona, naked-eye prominence, and spectacular diamond rings, followed by an unexpected sighting of dolphins.

articles.title: MS JUBLIEE, JULY 11, 1991 - Eclipse morning began eventfully.
articles.summary: On the morning of July 11, 1991, aboard the MS JUBLIEE cruising from Puerto Vallarta to Mazatlan, an observer experienced an eventful start to eclipse day. Hours before totality, a waterspout was sighted, followed by a sudden downpour that sent everyone scrambling to protect their equipment and 'shadow band sheets'.

articles.title: REPORT ON THE JULY 11, 1991 TOTAL ECLIPSE OF THE SUN
articles.summary: This report details Robert Garfinkle's experience observing the July 11, 1991 total solar eclipse from the Royal Caribbean cruise ship Viking Serenade off the coast of Baja California. Despite initial cloudy conditions, the ship navigated to a clear spot, allowing observers to witness the eclipse, including visible planets, prominences, and coronal streamers, along with a notable temperature drop. The author describes the unique observing conditions, comparing the darkness to a full moon night rather than complete darkness.

articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This article describes a personal account of observing a total solar eclipse, detailing the visual phenomena like sky darkening, color changes, and a temperature drop, along with a possible sighting of weak shadow bands. Post-totality observations included a school of dolphins and a rapid sky lightening, followed by a recap event with slides and videos from photographers Richard Berry and Richard Horowitz, and an endorsement from Edwin Krupp. The experience also highlights the camaraderie among eclipse chasers and stargazing education for novices.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article, "COMET COMMENTS" by Don Machholz, reports the recent recovery of two periodic comets: Wirtanen (1991s), recovered by T. Seki, and Hartley 2 (1991t), visually discovered by T. Kryachko, noting its early return. Additionally, it confirms that comet Levey (1991q) is now known to be periodic with a 50-year orbit.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document is a classifieds section titled "ASTRO ADS," offering free advertisements for noncommercial sales of astronomically related products or services. It features listings for used telescopes like Celestron 8s, Astro Physics refractors, Tele Vue Genesis, and Meade 2080 LX1s, along with various accessories and wanted ads for specific equipment. Ads are published for approximately three months after submission by the 15th of each month.

articles.title: OFFICERS AND DIRECTORS
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and directors of an organization, including their titles (President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, Editor, Director), names, and some contact phone numbers. It serves as a directory for the organization's leadership personnel.

articles.title: FREMONT PEAK STATE PARK
articles.summary: Fremont Peak State Park features a telescope observatory and offers various recreational activities including hiking on the 'Route of the Pioneers' trail and camping. The document provides visitor information such as routes, specific parking guidelines (with restrictions for larger vehicles), and park rules, emphasizing advance reservations for observation sites. It also mentions contact details for a park host and an educator.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP APPLICATION
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It details different membership options and their respective costs, including standard, standard with Sky & Telescope subscription, and junior memberships. The form also provides instructions for submission, either in person at an SJAA meeting or by mail to the treasurer.

articles.title: MAKE CHECKS PAYABLE TO "SJAA"
articles.summary: This document serves as a membership application/renewal form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for membership types and contact information. It also announces an upcoming 'Slide and Equipment Night' event on September 14th and provides submission guidelines for the SJAA's monthly publication, 'EPHEMERIS'.
